header: Problem 7 Explosive Chemistry. An explosion rapidly converts a system's energy into mechanical work through gas expansion, usually with intense heat, light, and sound. Explosive chemistry appears both as a laboratory hazard and in high-density energy-storage materials.

subquestions.text_open: 7-1-2 Isopropanol deterioration is modeled by acetone reacting in acid with equal numbers of H_2O_2 molecules: two acetone molecules give DADP and 3 give TATP. Both are highly symmetric peroxides. Give their SMILES.

rubric_images.description: DADP and TATP structures as listed. SMILES/structure strings shown: 'CC1(C)OOC(C)(C)OO1', 'CC1(C)OOC(C)(C)OOC(C)(C)OO1'.

subquestions.text_open: 7-1-3 One TATP first gives cyclic A plus acetone; A then gives acetone, dipolar B, and gas. Write 2 equations with A and B as SMILES.
rubric: No credit unless A and B are SMILES. 'CC1(OO1)C' and 'CC([O+])([O-])C' are not accepted for B.

subquestions.text_open: 7-1-4 DADP is unexpectedly much more stable than M. Lone-pair donation into a particular antibonding orbital controls the difference. Give limiting resonance-form SMILES for each and explain. No more than 100 words.
rubric: DADP: 'CC1(C)OOC(C)(C)OO1' ↔ '[O-]OC(C)(C)O/[O+]=C(C)/C'; M: 'CC1(C)CCC(C)(C)OO1' ↔ '[CH2-]CC(C)(C)O/[O+]=C(C)/C', or the listed methyl-anion alternative. (1 point each; carbocation forms accepted.) (2 points total.) Additional structure strings specified: 'CC1(C)CCC(C)(C)OO1', 'CC2=[O+]OC(C)(C)CC2.[CH3-]'.

O is more electronegative than C, so the O^- limiting form of DADP is more stable and gives greater stabilization. Equivalently, σ*(C-O) is lower than σ*(C-C) and hyperconjugates better with the O lone pair, reducing lone-pair repulsion. (2 points)

rubric_images.description: DADP and M resonance pairs as listed. SMILES/structure strings shown: 'CC1(C)OOC(C)(C)OO1', '[O-]OC(C)(C)O/[O+]=C(C)/C', 'CC1(C)CCC(C)(C)OO1', '[CH2-]CC(C)(C)O/[O+]=C(C)/C'.
Alternative M resonance pair with 'CC2=[O+]OC(C)(C)CC2.[CH3-]'. SMILES/structure strings shown: 'CC1(C)CCC(C)(C)OO1'.

subquestions.text_open: 7-2-2 If H_2O_2 is enclosed in the CL-20 cage, does sensitivity rise or fall? Explain briefly. (No more than 100 words.)
rubric: 7-2-2 It rises. (1 point) Heated H_2O_2 generates radicals that initiate rapid chain decomposition of CL-20. (1 point; radical generation or initiation of decomposition is sufficient.)

subquestions.text_open: 7-3 Thermal decomposition of condensed-phase CL-20 may proceed through a series of complex transformations. Initially, cleavage of an N-N bond in CL-20 generates NO_2, which then reacts with CL-20 and its remaining fragments through several pathways: (1) NO_2 oxidizes CL-20 to G. G may be represented by the formula CN-CHO. Homolytic bond cleavage and hydrogen-radical transfer by G produce the common small molecules H and I, of which H contains nitrogen. (2) NO_2 reacts with CL-20 to form J, which decomposes to a hydroxyl radical and K; K contains no carbon. 7-3-1 Give the SMILES representations of G (without formal charges), I, and J.
rubric: 7-3-1 G: '[C]=NC([H])=O'; I: '[C-]#[O+]'; J: 'O=NO[H]'. 5 points total: G and J are worth 2 points each, and I is worth 1 point. Each structure earns credit only if it is entirely correct.

subquestions.text_open: 7-3-2 Give two other reasonable resonance forms of G.

rubric_images.description: The two resonance forms. SMILES/structure strings shown: '[C-]#[N+]C([H])=O', '[C]=[N+]=C([H])[O-]'.

subquestions.text_open: 7-4 N-N bond cleavage is the rate-determining step in the early thermal decomposition of crystalline CL-20. To determine its activation energy $E_a$, researchers simulated CL-20 decomposition in a rigid container and obtained the initial $NO_2$ formation rates below. $T\ (\mathrm{K})$: 1488, 1969, 2547, 3124. $k\ (\mathrm{s^{-1}})$: $1.28\times10^9$, $1.54\times10^9$, $1.74\times10^9$, $1.89\times10^9$. 7-4-1 Treat N-N cleavage under the simulated conditions as a first-order reaction obeying the Arrhenius law. Calculate $E_a$ and the pre-exponential factor $A$, both to 2 significant figures.
rubric:
From the Arrhenius equation $k=Ae^{-E_a/(RT)}$, linearization gives $\ln k=-\dfrac{E_a}{RT}+\ln A$. (1 point; either the original or linearized equation earns credit.)

| \(1/T \, (\text{K}^{-1})\) | \(6.720 \times 10^{-4}\) | \(5.079 \times 10^{-4}\) | \(3.926 \times 10^{-4}\) | \(3.201 \times 10^{-4}\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(\ln k\) | 20.97 | 21.16 | 21.28 | 21.36 |

(1 point; at least one type of data must be processed, otherwise no credit is awarded for this step.) $\ln k=-1.10\times10^3/T+21.7$. (2 points) Therefore $E_a=9.2\ \mathrm{kJ\cdot mol^{-1}}$ and $A=2.7\times10^9\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. (2 points)

subquestions.text_open: 7-4-3 The simulated pre-exponential factor is four orders of magnitude below experiment for CL-20 under real explosion conditions. Give 1 principal reason based on the setup. No more than 100 words.
rubric: The simulation uses a rigid container of constant volume, whereas the volume of a real explosion increases rapidly; equivalently, the fixed volume keeps the local concentration of gaseous products higher than in a real explosion. (1 point; the complete explanation is required.)
